title: Infostop
text: vignette demonstrates two-stage Infostop workflow R. first stage identifies stationary events (identify_stops()), second stage groups nearby events recurring sites (identify_sites()).

title: Infostop
text: NA labels represent points assigned stop site. main parameters can changed independently two stages:
code: stops <- identify_stops(path_trackframe) sites <- identify_sites(stops)  head(stops$stop_id) ## [1] 1 1 1 1 1 1 head(sites$site_id) ## [1] 1 1 1 1 1 1 stops <- identify_stops(   path_trackframe,   r1 = 10,   min_size = 2L,   min_staying_time = 300 )  sites <- identify_sites(   stops,   r2 = 10,   label_singleton = TRUE,   weighted = FALSE )

title: Detect Stop Locations in Mobility Data
text: package provides R wrapper Python ‘infostop’ package, implements algorithms detecting stop locations time-ordered location data. package useful anyone wishes detect stationary events location coordinate streams, simplifying dense rich location time-series sequences events. underlying algorithm described Aslak et al. (2020).

title: Detect Stop Locations in Mobility Data
text: can install development version infostop GitHub: package requires Python ‘infostop’ package. can install using:
code: devtools::install_github("yourusername/infostop") library(infostop) install_infostop()

title: Detect Stop Locations in Mobility Data
code: library(infostop)  # Create a model model <- infostop(r1 = 10, r2 = 10)  # Example data (latitude, longitude, timestamp) data <- matrix(c(   55.75259295, 12.34353885, 1581401760,   55.7525908, 12.34353145, 1581402760,   55.7525876, 12.3435386, 1581403760,   63.40379175, 10.40477095, 1583401760,   63.4037841, 10.40480265, 1583402760,   63.403787, 10.4047871, 1583403760 ), ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)  # Fit the model and predict labels labels <- model$fit_predict_r(data)  # Plot the map (if you have folium installed in Python) map <- plot_map(model)

title: Detect Stop Locations in Mobility Data
text: Simplicity: core, method works two steps. (1) Reducing location trace medians stationary event (2) embedding resulting locations network connects locations within user-defined distance clustering network. Multi-trace support: Supports clustering multiple traces find global stop locations. Flow based: Spatial clusters correspond collections location points contain large amounts flow represented network. enables recovery locations traces slightly overlap. Speed: First point space reduced median stationary points, spatially neighboring points connected using Ball search tree algorithm, finally network clustered using C++ based Infomap program.
